name: University course
description: Pass a university course with a calm, steady plan: map the syllabus, study each unit as it is taught, practise with past exams and arrive at the final exam prepared. Set the goal's deadline to your exam date.

steps.title: Read the syllabus and set up the term
steps.description: Note the grading scheme, deadlines, required readings, office hours and the exam date. Find out what the exam looks like.

steps.title: Plan the term in your calendar
steps.description: Put every lecture, assignment and exam in your calendar and reserve fixed weekly study blocks for this course.

steps.title: Unit 1: study and exercises
steps.description: Read before the lecture, take notes in class, rewrite them the same day and solve the exercises for the unit.

steps.title: Unit 2: study and exercises
steps.description: Read before the lecture, take notes in class, rewrite them the same day and solve the exercises for the unit.

steps.title: Unit 3: study and exercises
steps.description: Read before the lecture, take notes in class, rewrite them the same day and solve the exercises for the unit.

steps.title: Midterm preparation
steps.description: Review units 1 to 3 with active recall, solve a past midterm under time pressure and fix the gaps.

steps.title: Unit 4: study and exercises
steps.description: Read before the lecture, take notes in class, rewrite them the same day and solve the exercises for the unit.

steps.title: Unit 5: study and exercises
steps.description: Read before the lecture, take notes in class, rewrite them the same day and solve the exercises for the unit.

steps.title: Assignments and projects
steps.description: Start each assignment as soon as it is announced, finish a draft early and use office hours for the parts you are stuck on.

steps.title: Past exams and exam-style practice
steps.description: Solve as many past exams as you can find, in exam conditions. Mark them strictly and list the topics behind each lost point.

steps.title: Consolidation: summary sheets and concept maps
steps.description: Condense the course into one-page summaries, formula sheets or concept maps you could rebuild from memory.

steps.title: Final exam week
steps.description: Alternate full past papers with targeted review of weak topics, keep sleeping and eating well and stop studying the evening before.

competencies.name: Understanding of concepts
competencies.description: Explain the core ideas of the course in your own words and connect them to each other.

competencies.name: Problem solving
competencies.description: Solve new exercises of the types the exam uses, within the time limit.

competencies.name: Written explanations
competencies.description: Justify answers clearly and completely, the way the marking scheme rewards.

competencies.name: Exam technique
competencies.description: Plan the time, choose the order of questions and check answers before handing in.

competencies.name: Study habits
competencies.description: Keep a steady weekly rhythm of reading, review and practice instead of cramming.

routines.title: Weekly review of the whole course

cards.back: Testing yourself without looking at your notes. It beats rereading because retrieving a memory strengthens it.
Reviewing material at growing intervals (1 day, 3 days, 1 week...) just before you would forget it, so it sticks for much less total time.
Explain the concept in plain words as if teaching a beginner. Wherever you stumble is what you still have to study.
Work in focused blocks of about 25 minutes separated by 5-minute breaks, with a longer break every four blocks.
Mixing different topics or problem types in one study session instead of repeating a single type. It feels harder and works better.
They show what the exam really asks, at which depth and in which format, so you can aim your studying at it.

cards.front: How do you use a mistake?
cards.back: Write down the correct method and the reason you went wrong, then redo the problem a few days later without looking.
